items.followUp: Describe the dark reactions of photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Identifies where light reactions occur and that they require light.
rubric.how: Award for stating that light reactions take place in the grana (thylakoid membranes) in the presence of light.

rubric.why: Explains how the light energy is captured.
rubric.how: Award for stating that chlorophyll absorbs light energy.

rubric.why: Names the splitting of water and its products.
rubric.how: Award for describing the splitting of water and identifying oxygen as a product.

rubric.why: Identifies the energy-rich products formed in the light reactions.
rubric.how: Award for naming ATP and NADPH as products; accept either one for this mark.

rubric.why: States the fate of oxygen produced by photolysis.
rubric.how: Award for stating that oxygen is released, for example into the atmosphere.

modelAnswer: Light reactions are the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis that take place in the grana in the presence of light.
This energy is used to split water into hydrogen and oxygen; this process is called photolysis.
Oxygen is released into the atmosphere.

rubric.why: A definition of morphology must identify it as the study of the form or structure of organisms.
rubric.how: Award both marks for defining morphology as the study of the form and structure of organisms; award one mark if only form or structure is correctly identified.

modelAnswer: Morphology is the study of the form and structure of organisms.

rubric.why: The zone of life is the part or region of Earth where life exists.
rubric.description: Part of Earth where life exists
rubric.how: Award both marks for identifying it as the part or region of Earth where life exists; award one mark for identifying it as a region of Earth without stating that life exists there.

modelAnswer: The zone of life is the part of Earth where life exists; it is called the biosphere.

items.followUp: Write down two characteristics of a scientific theory.

rubric.why: A hypothesis must be capable of being tested.
rubric.how: Award for stating that a hypothesis can be tested.

rubric.why: A hypothesis is a provisional explanation for an observation or problem.
rubric.how: Award for stating that a hypothesis is a tentative, possible, or proposed explanation.

modelAnswer: A hypothesis is a tentative explanation for an observation or problem.

rubric.why: The biological method is an organised procedure for solving problems.
rubric.how: Award for identifying it as a systematic or step-by-step method.

rubric.why: The method is used to investigate or solve problems in biology.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the method is used to investigate or solve biological problems.

modelAnswer: The biological method is a systematic way of investigating and solving biological problems.

items.followUp: What is the function of plasmodesmata?

rubric.why: Plasmodesmata are channels connecting neighbouring plant cells through their walls.
rubric.how: Award for identifying them as channels or pores between adjacent plant cells.

rubric.why: These connections link the cytoplasm of neighbouring cells and allow transport or communication.
rubric.how: Award for stating that they connect the cytoplasm through the cell wall or allow transport/communication between cells.

modelAnswer: Plasmodesmata are microscopic channels that pass through the cell walls of adjacent plant cells.
They connect the cells' cytoplasm and allow transport and communication between them.

items.followUp: What happens to a plant cell placed in a hypotonic solution?

rubric.why: Plasmolysis involves the protoplast shrinking away from the cell wall.
rubric.description: Protoplast pulls away from cell wall
rubric.how: Award for describing the shrinkage of the protoplast and its separation from the cell wall.

rubric.why: This occurs when a plant cell loses water in a hypertonic solution.
rubric.how: Award for linking plasmolysis to water loss in a hypertonic solution.

modelAnswer: Plasmolysis is the shrinkage of a plant cell's protoplast away from the cell wall.
It occurs when the cell loses water in a hypertonic solution.

items.followUp: Write down two aims of taxonomy.

rubric.why: Identifying organisms is one aim of classification.
rubric.how: Award for stating that classification helps identify organisms.

rubric.why: Classification groups organisms, commonly according to their similarities and differences.
rubric.how: Award for stating that classification groups organisms, preferably according to similarities and differences.

modelAnswer: It groups organisms according to their similarities and differences.
